# Version numbers

This page is for developers who release a site package or a package it requires. A package has several version
fields, and they do different jobs: one decides whether a requirement is met, one is only shown, one is not read at
all. Getting them right matters most for packages that other packages require, because the setup wizard compares
versions to decide whether to download a package again.

## Contents

1. [The version fields](#the-version-fields)
2. [How a package version is read](#how-a-package-version-is-read)
3. [What the shipped packages use](#what-the-shipped-packages-use)
4. [Traps](#traps)
5. [Recommended form](#recommended-form)
6. [Related pages](#related-pages)

## The version fields

| Field | Where | Used for | Enforced |
|---|---|---|---|
| Version number | `<version><number>` | The package version, joined with the release | Must be a plain token, up to 64 of `0-9 A-Z a-z . _ + -` |
| Release | `<version><release>` | The second half of the package version | The same token rule |
| Product version | `<ezpublish><version>` and `<named-version>` | Shown as "For Exponential" on the package page | Only that `<ezpublish>` exists (on `package/upload`) |
| Format version | `version` attribute of `<package>` | Nothing: `parseDOMTree()` does not read it | No |
| Index version | `version` attribute in `index.xml` | Shown on the setup wizard's site type step; compared with an imported package | No |

The token rule is `eZPackage::isValidDefinitionToken()` in `kernel/classes/ezpackage.php`; a definition that breaks
it is not read at all ([Required package.xml fields](package-xml-required-fields.md)).

## How a package version is read

`eZPackage::getVersion()` joins the two halves with a hyphen: `<number>-<release>`. This pair is what
`min-version` in a `<require>` is compared with, and what the setup wizard compares between an imported package and
the index. The comparison is `eZPackageVersion::compareFull()` in `kernel/classes/ezpackageversion.php`:

1. The part after the **last** hyphen is the release number only when it is **all digits**. `1.0-1` is version
   `1.0`, release `1`. Otherwise the whole text is the version number, with no release.
2. Version numbers compare by Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 precedence. Older forms are read too: `1` and `1.0` as
   `1.0.0`, `1.2.3.4` with the fourth part after PATCH, `3.4.0beta1` as the prerelease `beta1`.
3. A version with a prerelease comes **before** the same version without one. Prerelease identifiers compare one by
   one: numeric ones numerically, others in ASCII order.
4. The release numbers compare last, numerically, a missing one as `0`: `1.0-1` < `1.0-2` < `1.0.1-1`.

## What the shipped packages use

Checked in the two 7x source repositories on 2026-10-18:

| Packages | `<number>` | `<release>` | `<ezpublish><version>` |
|---|---|---|---|
| The 5 site packages, `cjw_multisite_democontent`, both `sevenx_multisite_democontent` packages | `6.0` | `15-stable` | `6.0.15-stable` |
| `sevenx_democontent` | `6.0` | `14-stable` | `6.0.14-stable` |
| `sevenx_banners`, `sevenx_classes`, `sevenx_democontent_clean`, the three `sevenx_design_*` | `6.0` | `10-stable` | `6.0.10-stable` |
| `sevenx_extension` | `6.0` | `6.0.15-stable` | `6.0.15-stable` |

The release follows the patch number of an Exponential 6.0 release (10, 14, 15), the same release `<ezpublish><version>` names. The site packages require their
dependencies with `min-version="5.1"` or `min-version="1.0"`, and in the 6.0.15 `index.xml` the 7x site packages
are listed with `version="1.0.0-0"`.

## Traps

**A release with a state word (fixed in 6.0.15).** From 6.0.15 on, `compareFull()` reads digits followed by a state
word as a release: `6.0-15-stable` (and `6.0-15stable`) is version `6.0`, release `15`. A stable word (`stable`,
`final`, `release`, `ga`) means no prerelease, so `6.0-15-stable` equals `6.0-15` and meets a `min-version="6.0"`.
Any other word makes a prerelease of that release: `6.0-15-rc1` < `6.0-15`. The same stable words after a legacy
version number (`6.0.15stable`, `1.0-final`) are not a prerelease either.

> **Note**
> Before 6.0.15 a release that was not all digits was no release: `6.0-15-stable` was read as the version `6.0.0`
> with the prerelease `15-stable`, lower than `6.0`, so a `min-version="6.0"` was **not** met, and the wizard treated
> the imported package as too old. Releases also compared as text then (`9-stable` above `15-stable`); from 6.0.15
> on they compare as numbers. An installation older than 6.0.15 still reads them the old way, so a package meant for
> one should keep asking for `5.1` or `1.0`, as the shipped site packages do.

**The index version is compared too.** When the index lists a higher version than an imported package has, the
site type step offers the index entry instead of the imported one (`eZStepSiteTypes::createSitePackagesList()`).
In kickstart mode the index entry is always preferred. Keep the index version equal to the package's
`<number>-<release>`.

**The product version is not a compatibility check.** Nothing compares `<ezpublish><version>` with the running
release. Say in the description and the source repository's README which releases a package is meant for.

## Recommended form

For a new package or a new release of your own:

- [ ] `<number>`: Semantic Versioning, three numbers (`1.0.0`, `1.2.0`). The creation wizards insist on this: at
      most 24 characters, because the `ezpackage` table stores `<number>-<release>` in 30
      (`eZPackageVersion::MAX_NEW_LENGTH`).
- [ ] `<release>`: a whole number, `1` for the first build of a version, raised when the same version is
      packaged again.
- [ ] `<ezpublish><version>`: the Exponential release you built and tested it on, such as `6.0.15-stable`, with
      `<named-version>6.0</named-version>`.
- [ ] The `version` attribute in `index.xml`: the same `<number>-<release>`.
- [ ] The changelog entry's `release` attribute: the same release ([Changelog entries](changelog-entries.md)).
- [ ] A `min-version` in a site package that names a version the required package really has, written the same way.

```xml
<version>
  <number>1.2.0</number>
  <release>1</release>
</version>
```

How to number your own releases over time is on [Versioning your own packages](../your-own/versioning-your-own-packages.md).
The settings and the wizard side are in
[Package licenses and Semantic Versioning](../../../features/6.0/package-licenses-and-versions.md).
